rows.rbnz_series_mapping: RBNZ Table C41 (FHB borrower-weighted average gross income)
rows.hlf_calculation: $383.0m total FHB gross income pool × $1m ÷ 2,655.4 implied FHB applications = $144,232
rows.summary_text: In September 2026, the typical (borrower-weighted average) gross household income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications was $144,232 (down 0.2% year-on-year from $144,534 a year earlier).

rows.rbnz_series_mapping: RBNZ Table C31 (Total FHB new lending value ÷ FHB loan count)
rows.summary_text: In September 2026, the average first-home buyer mortgage approved across New Zealand was $573,678 (up 0.1% year-on-year from $573,095 a year earlier), across 2,667 first-home buyer loans totalling $1.53B ($1,530m).

rows.rbnz_series_mapping: RBNZ Tables C31, C40 & C41 (Implied FHB loan-to-income ratio & share ≤ 6x TDTI)
rows.hlf_calculation: Implied FHB Loan-to-Income Ratio: $573,678 (C31 avg FHB loan) ÷ $144,232 (C41 avg FHB gross income) = 3.98x | C40 Share <= 6x TDTI: 100.0% − 9.0% = 91.0% (Share <= 5x TDTI: 65.0%)
rows.summary_text: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyers borrowed an implied mortgage-to-income multiple of 3.98x gross income ($573,678 average loan on $144,232 average gross income), with 91.0% of all first-home buyer lending written at or below 6x TDTI (and 65.0% at or below 5x TDTI).

rows.rbnz_series_mapping: RBNZ Table C40 (FHB DTI > 6x share vs. 20% RBNZ speed limit)
rows.summary_text: In September 2026, 9.0% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($137.0m of $1,525.0m)—sitting 11.0 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.

rows.rbnz_series_mapping: RBNZ Table C31 (Monthly new FHB mortgage commitments & loan count)
rows.summary_text: In September 2026, New Zealand banks committed $1.53B ($1,530m) in new first-home buyer mortgages across 2,667 loans (down 2.7% year-on-year from $1.57B ($1,572m) across 2,743 loans a year earlier).

townhouse-share.html: In September 2026, 51.5% (1,837 of 3,570) of new residential dwelling consents were for multi-unit homes—with townhouses, flats, and units accounting for 36.6% (1,305) and apartments plus retirement village units accounting for 14.9% (532).
townhouse-share.official_data_summary: Stats NZ Building Consents (September 2026): Total dwellings = 3,570; Stand-alone houses = 1,733; Townhouses, flats & units = 1,305; Apartments & retirement units = 532.
townhouse-share.source_html:
HLF calculation: Multi-unit overall: (3,570 − 1,733) ÷ 3,570 = 1,837 ÷ 3,570 = 51.5% | Townhouses/flats/units: 1,305 ÷ 3,570 = 36.6%
Source: Stats NZ — Building Consents Issued (Monthly Information Release) • Glossary: Turnkey vs Construction Loan • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

townhouse-share.definition: The percentage of monthly new residential dwelling consents issued for multi-unit homes overall (townhouses, flats, units, apartments, and retirement village units) and specifically for townhouses, flats, and units.
townhouse-share.formula: Multi-Unit Share = ((Total Consents - Stand-Alone Houses) ÷ Total Consents) × 100; Townhouse/Flat/Unit Share = (Townhouses, Flats & Units ÷ Total Consents) × 100
townhouse-share.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Multi-unit homes—led by townhouses—now represent roughly half of all new dwellings consented in New Zealand, particularly in main urban centres.
townhouse-share.methodology: Derived from Stats NZ Building Consents Issued by subtracting stand-alone houses from total new dwellings consented and dividing by total new dwellings consented, alongside the separate share for townhouses, flats, and units.
townhouse-share.summary_text: In September 2026, 51.5% (1,837 of 3,570) of new residential dwelling consents were for multi-unit homes—with townhouses, flats, and units accounting for 36.6% (1,305) and apartments plus retirement village units accounting for 14.9% (532).

rent-yield-pulse.html: In September 2026, New Zealand's national median weekly private rent was $599/wk (up 1.5% year-on-year), with regional medians of $640/wk in Auckland, $580/wk in Wellington, and $560/wk in Canterbury.
rent-yield-pulse.official_data_summary: MBIE Tenancy Services (September 2026): National ('ALL') median weekly rent = $599/wk; Auckland = $640/wk; Wellington = $580/wk; Canterbury = $560/wk.
rent-yield-pulse.source_html:
HLF calculation: Reported national median = $599/wk; YoY = ($599 - $590) ÷ $590 = +1.5%
Source: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — Tenancy Services Rental Bond Data • Glossary: Gross Rental Yield • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

rent-long-term-growth.html: Over the 10 years to September 2026, New Zealand's national median weekly rent rose +53.6% (+$209/wk, or +4.4%/yr) from $390/wk to $599/wk. Over the past 5 years (from $495/wk), median rent rose +21.0% (+3.9%/yr).

HLF calculation: 10Y Nominal: ($599−$390)÷$390=+53.6% (+4.4%/yr) | 5Y Nominal: ($599−$495)÷$495=+21.0% (+3.9%/yr)
Source: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — Tenancy Services Rental Bond Data • Glossary: Gross Rental Yield • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

rent-quartile-spread.html: In September 2026, New Zealand private weekly rents ranged from $495/wk at the lower quartile (25th percentile) and $599/wk at the national median to $700/wk at the upper quartile (75th percentile)—a spread of $205/wk ($10,660/yr).
rent-quartile-spread.official_data_summary: MBIE Tenancy Services (September 2026): Nationwide ('ALL') Lower Quartile Rent = $495/wk; Median Rent = $599/wk; Upper Quartile Rent = $700/wk.
rent-quartile-spread.source_html:
HLF calculation: Upper Quartile ($700/wk) minus Lower Quartile ($495/wk) = $205/wk ($10,660/yr)
Source: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — Tenancy Services Rental Bond Data • Glossary: Gross Rental Yield • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

rent-quartile-spread.formula: Interquartile Spread ($/wk) = Upper Quartile Rent minus Lower Quartile Rent; Annualised Spread = Spread × 52
rent-quartile-spread.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Shows the weekly cashflow difference between entry-level units/flats (lower quartile) and larger family homes (upper quartile).
rent-quartile-spread.methodology: Sourced from MBIE Tenancy Services' regional bond CSV (Location = 'ALL'), subtracting Lower Quartile Rent from Upper Quartile Rent and multiplying by 52 for the annualised spread.

investor-equity-tiers.source_published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end)

investor-equity-tiers.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): Total investors = 2,668; <=60% LVR = 1,169; >60% LVR = 1,499; >70% LVR = 527 ($337m).
investor-equity-tiers.source_html:
HLF calculation: <=60% LVR: 1,169 ÷ 2,668 = 43.8% | 60–70% LVR: 972 ÷ 2,668 = 36.4% | >70% LVR: 527 ÷ 2,668 = 19.8%
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

investor-equity-tiers.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31)
investor-equity-tiers.source_series_ids: LVRN.MMB2.TN (<=60% LVR) | LVRN.MMB2.FN - DN (60–70% LVR) | LVRN.MMB2.DN (>70% LVR)

investor-equity-tiers.formula: <=60% LVR = TN ÷ AN; 60–70% LVR = (FN - DN) ÷ AN; >70% LVR = DN ÷ AN
investor-equity-tiers.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Shows how investor borrowing clusters across the 60% and 70% LVR thresholds, with >70% LVR lending largely reflecting LVR-exempt new-build investment properties.
investor-equity-tiers.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 investor borrower count series LVRN.MMB2.TN (<=60% LVR), LVRN.MMB2.FN (>60% LVR), LVRN.MMB2.DN (>70% LVR), and LVRN.MMB2.AN (total investors).
investor-equity-tiers.summary_text: In September 2026, 43.8% of property investor mortgages were written with at least 40% equity (≤60% LVR, 1,169 loans), 36.4% with 30%–40% equity (60%–70% LVR, 972 loans), and 19.8% with under 30% equity (>70% LVR, 527 loans / $337m).

Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

investor-low-deposit.definition: Monthly count and dollar value of residential property investor mortgage commitments approved at >80% LVR (under 20% deposit) and in the 70%–80% LVR band (20%–30% deposit).
investor-low-deposit.formula: >80% LVR = LVRN.MMB2.BN; 70%–80% LVR = LVRN.MMB2.DN minus LVRN.MMB2.BN
investor-low-deposit.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Under RBNZ LVR rules, new builds are exempt from LVR speed limits, allowing eligible new-build investors to borrow at 80% LVR (a 20% deposit) alongside discretionary bank speed-limit allowances.
investor-low-deposit.methodology: Extracted from RBNZ Table C31 series LVRN.MMB2.BN / LVRN.MMB1.BN (>80% LVR investors), with the 70%–80% LVR band derived by subtracting >80% LVR investor commitments from >70% LVR investor commitments (LVRN.MMB2.DN / LVRN.MMB1.DN).
investor-low-deposit.summary_text: In September 2026, 52 property investor mortgages ($36m) were approved with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR, or 1.9% of investors, up from 34 loans a year earlier) (508 loans / $328m over the past 12 months), alongside 475 investor loans ($301m, or 17.8%) in the 70%–80% LVR band.

refinance.source_published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end)
refinance.html: In September 2026, 2,772 New Zealand mortgage holders switched lenders, refinancing $1.73B ($1,729m) in home loans—representing 23.0% of all new residential mortgage lending, at an average loan size of $623,737.
refinance.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Change in loan provider = 2,772 borrowers and $1,729m out of $7,533m total purpose lending.
refinance.source_html:
HLF calculation: $1,729m ÷ $7,533m = 23.0% (Mean loan: $1,729m × $1m ÷ 2,772 = $623,737)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33) • Direct RBNZ C33 .xlsx • Glossary: Refinancing · Usable Equity • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
refinance.name: Mortgage refinancing (switching loan provider) share & volume
refinance.also_known_as: Bank-to-bank mortgage switching share, loan count & average refinance size
refinance.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33)
refinance.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived share/mean
refinance.definition: The share of new residential mortgage lending value and number of borrowers switching from one mortgage lender to another ('change in loan provider'), alongside the mean refinanced loan size.
refinance.formula: (Change in Loan Provider Value [LVRN.MMB1.AZD] ÷ Total Lending by Purpose) × 100; Mean Loan = LVRN.MMB1.AZD ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AZD
refinance.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Refinancing volume measures how actively existing mortgage holders are comparing fixed rates and cashback offers across competing banks once their fixed terms expire.
refinance.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C33 by dividing 'change in loan provider' lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AZD) by the sum of all purpose categories (property purchase AZC, top-up AZB, change in provider AZD, and other AZE).
refinance.summary_text: In September 2026, 2,772 New Zealand mortgage holders switched lenders, refinancing $1.73B ($1,729m) in home loans—representing 23.0% of all new residential mortgage lending, at an average loan size of $623,737.

top-ups.source_published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end)
top-ups.html: In September 2026, 9,639 homeowners were approved for a mortgage top-up on their existing property—accounting for 46.4% of all mortgage approvals across New Zealand, with an average top-up of $99,803.
top-ups.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Top-up approvals = 9,639 borrowers ($962m) out of 20,763 total approvals.
top-ups.source_html:
HLF calculation: 9,639 ÷ 20,763 = 46.4% (Mean top-up: $962m × $1m ÷ 9,639 = $99,803)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33) • Direct RBNZ C33 .xlsx • Glossary: Refinancing · Usable Equity • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
top-ups.name: Mortgage top-up share of approvals & average top-up amount

top-ups.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33)
top-ups.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived share/mean
top-ups.definition: The percentage of all monthly residential mortgage approvals that are top-ups on an existing mortgage with the same lender, alongside the mean dollar top-up size.
top-ups.formula: (Top-up Count [LVRN.MMB2.AZB] ÷ Total Approvals by Purpose) × 100; Mean Top-Up = LVRN.MMB1.AZB ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AZB
top-ups.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Top-ups are one of the most common transactions in New Zealand banking—used by homeowners to fund renovations, deposits on investment properties, or major capital purchases.
top-ups.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C33 by dividing top-up borrower count (LVRN.MMB2.AZB) by total mortgage approvals across all purposes, and dividing top-up lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AZB, rounded to $1m) by top-up borrower count.
top-ups.summary_text: In September 2026, 9,639 homeowners were approved for a mortgage top-up on their existing property—accounting for 46.4% of all mortgage approvals across New Zealand, with an average top-up of $99,803.

dti-headroom.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $137.0m out of $1,525.0m total FHB commitments.
dti-headroom.source_html:
HLF calculation: $137.0m ÷ $1,525.0m = 9.0% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.0% = 11.0 pts)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40) • Direct RBNZ C40 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

dti-headroom.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40)
dti-headroom.source_series_ids: FHB New Commitments with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB New Commitments
dti-headroom.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived >6x DTI share
dti-headroom.definition: The percentage of total monthly first-home buyer mortgage lending value committed at a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x gross income, compared against the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap on non-exempt owner-occupier lending.
dti-headroom.formula: (FHB Lending with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB Commitments across all TDTI bands) × 100; Headroom = 20.0% minus (>6x Share)
dti-headroom.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because bank test servicing rates already constrain borrowing capacity, total FHB lending above 6x DTI sits well inside the 20% RBNZ speed-limit allowance.
dti-headroom.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C40 by summing first-home buyer lending commitments in bands above 6x TDTI (including unknown TDTI) and dividing by total first-home buyer commitments across all TDTI bands.
dti-headroom.summary_text: In September 2026, 9.0% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($137.0m of $1,525.0m)—sitting 11.0 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.

borrower-income.source_published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end)
borrower-income.html: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands).
borrower-income.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Figures: TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 avg ($59.0m pool / 299.5 implied apps) | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 avg ($101.0m pool / 668.9 implied apps) | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 avg ($124.0m pool / 892.1 implied apps) | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 avg ($76.0m pool / 608.0 implied apps) | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000 avg ($23.0m pool / 187.0 implied apps).
borrower-income.source_html:
HLF calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41) • Direct RBNZ C41 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
borrower-income.calculation_live: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232

borrower-income.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41)
borrower-income.source_series_ids: Sum(Band Total Gross Income) ÷ Sum(Band Implied Borrowers) across TDTI bands
borrower-income.data_type: HLF-derived band-weighted mean from official RBNZ Table C41 bands
borrower-income.definition: The band-weighted mean annual gross borrower income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications and property investor applications, derived by HLF from RBNZ Table C41's Debt-to-Income bands.
borrower-income.calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232
borrower-income.formula: Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m]) ÷ Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m] ÷ Band Average Gross Income [$k]) × 1,000
borrower-income.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: RBNZ's Borrower Gross Income (BGI) measures total application income (which for couples combines two salaries, and for investors includes existing salaries plus gross rental and other qualifying income).
borrower-income.methodology: RBNZ Table C41 publishes official total gross income ($m, rounded to $0.1m) and average gross income ($000, rounded to $1,000) within each TDTI band rather than a single all-bands average. HLF derives the overall mean by dividing total gross income summed across all reported TDTI bands by the implied number of applications (Band Total Income ÷ Band Average Income) summed across those bands.
borrower-income.summary_text: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands).
borrower-income.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors," September 2026. fhb-typical-income.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because most first-home buyers apply as a couple (or with co-borrowers), RBNZ Borrower Gross Income reflects combined household income on the mortgage application.
fhb-typical-income.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C41 by summing total gross borrower income ($m) across all five first-home buyer Debt-to-Income bands and dividing by the total implied number of applications across those bands.

fhb-typical-dti.html: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyers borrowed an implied mortgage-to-income multiple of 3.98x gross income ($573,678 average loan on $144,232 average gross income), with 91.0% of all first-home buyer lending written at or below 6x TDTI (and 65.0% at or below 5x TDTI).
fhb-typical-dti.official_data_summary: RBNZ Tables C31, C40 & C41 (September 2026): Average FHB loan = $573,678; Average FHB gross income = $144,232; FHB lending <= 6x TDTI = 91.0% (<= 5x TDTI = 65.0%; > 6x TDTI = 9.0%).
fhb-typical-dti.source_html:
HLF calculation: Implied FHB Loan-to-Income Ratio: $573,678 (C31 avg FHB loan) ÷ $144,232 (C41 avg FHB gross income) = 3.98x | C40 Share <= 6x TDTI: 100.0% − 9.0% = 91.0% (Share <= 5x TDTI: 65.0%)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New Lending (C31), DTI Purpose Use (C40) & Borrower Gross Income (C41) • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) · Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-typical-dti.definition: The implied mortgage-to-income multiple for approved New Zealand first-home buyers (average FHB loan size in Table C31 divided by average FHB gross borrower income in Table C41), alongside the proportion of FHB lending written at or below 5x and 6x Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) in RBNZ Table C40.
fhb-typical-dti.calculation: Implied FHB Loan-to-Income Ratio: $573,678 (C31 avg FHB loan) ÷ $144,232 (C41 avg FHB gross income) = 3.98x | C40 Share <= 6x TDTI: 100.0% − 9.0% = 91.0% (Share <= 5x TDTI: 65.0%)
fhb-typical-dti.formula: Implied Mortgage-to-Income Ratio = Avg FHB Loan (C31) ÷ Avg FHB Gross Income (C41); Share <= 6x TDTI = 100% − (>6x TDTI Share in C40)
fhb-typical-dti.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Most New Zealand first-home buyers borrow around 3.9x to 4.1x their gross household income in mortgage debt—well below the 6.0x RBNZ owner-occupier speed-limit threshold—because bank servicing test rates cap borrowing capacity before the 6x DTI limit is reached.
fhb-typical-dti.methodology: Divides the monthly mean FHB mortgage size (RBNZ Table C31) by the monthly band-weighted mean FHB gross borrower income (RBNZ Table C41), paired with the official share of FHB commitments in TDTI bands <= 5x and <= 6x from RBNZ Table C40.

natural-hazard-claims.html: The Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake (NHC) provides statutory first-loss residential building cover up to $300,000 + GST ($345,000 incl. GST) per dwelling at an annual levy capped at $480 + GST ($552.00 incl. GST), following $3.8B+ in insured losses from the 2023 North Island severe weather events.

HLF calculation: Cap incl. GST: $300,000 × 1.15 = $345,000 | Max Levy incl. GST: ($300,000 ÷ 100 × $0.16) × 1.15 = $552.00
Source: Natural Hazards Insurance Act 2023 (NZ Legislation) & Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake (NHC) • Glossary: Sum Insured & Income Protection • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

acc-earners-levy-cap.methodology: Live-parsed from the official ACC and Inland Revenue PAYE / Earners' Levy schedule, multiplying the Maximum Liable Earnings cap by the GST-inclusive levy rate and by the 80% statutory weekly compensation rate.
acc-earners-levy-cap.summary_text: For the 2026/27 tax year, the ACC Earners' Levy is $1.75 per $100 (1.75% incl. GST) up to a Maximum Liable Earnings cap of $156,641 (a maximum annual levy of $2,741.22), capping ACC's 80% weekly compensation at $125,312.80/year ($2,409.86/week gross).

fhb-dti-above-6x.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $137.0m out of $1,525.0m total FHB commitments.
fhb-dti-above-6x.source_html:
HLF calculation: $137.0m ÷ $1,525.0m = 9.0% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.0% = 11.0 pts)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40) • Direct RBNZ C40 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-dti-above-6x.definition: The percentage of total monthly first-home buyer mortgage lending value committed at a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x gross income, compared against the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap on non-exempt owner-occupier lending.
fhb-dti-above-6x.formula: (FHB Lending with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB Commitments across all TDTI bands) × 100; Headroom = 20.0% minus (>6x Share)
fhb-dti-above-6x.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because bank test servicing rates already constrain borrowing capacity, total FHB lending above 6x DTI sits well inside the 20% RBNZ speed-limit allowance.
fhb-dti-above-6x.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C40 by summing first-home buyer lending commitments in bands above 6x TDTI (including unknown TDTI) and dividing by total first-home buyer commitments across all TDTI bands.
fhb-dti-above-6x.summary_text: In September 2026, 9.0% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($137.0m of $1,525.0m)—sitting 11.0 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.

fhb-typical-loan-size.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 by dividing monthly first-home buyer new lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AC1, published rounded to $1m) by monthly first-home buyer loan count (LVRN.MMB2.AC1).

fhb-dti-headroom.source_published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end)
fhb-dti-headroom.html: In September 2026, 9.0% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($137.0m of $1,525.0m)—sitting 11.0 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.

fhb-dti-headroom.source_html:
HLF calculation: $137.0m ÷ $1,525.0m = 9.0% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.0% = 11.0 pts)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40) • Direct RBNZ C40 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-dti-headroom.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived >6x DTI share
fhb-dti-headroom.definition: The percentage of total monthly first-home buyer mortgage lending value committed at a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x gross income, compared against the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap on non-exempt owner-occupier lending.
fhb-dti-headroom.formula: (FHB Lending with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB Commitments across all TDTI bands) × 100; Headroom = 20.0% minus (>6x Share)
fhb-dti-headroom.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because bank test servicing rates already constrain borrowing capacity, total FHB lending above 6x DTI sits well inside the 20% RBNZ speed-limit allowance.
fhb-dti-headroom.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C40 by summing first-home buyer lending commitments in bands above 6x TDTI (including unknown TDTI) and dividing by total first-home buyer commitments across all TDTI bands.
fhb-dti-headroom.summary_text: In September 2026, 9.0% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($137.0m of $1,525.0m)—sitting 11.0 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.

fhb-borrower-income.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Figures: TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 avg ($59.0m pool / 299.5 implied apps) | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 avg ($101.0m pool / 668.9 implied apps) | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 avg ($124.0m pool / 892.1 implied apps) | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 avg ($76.0m pool / 608.0 implied apps) | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000 avg ($23.0m pool / 187.0 implied apps).

HLF calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41) • Direct RBNZ C41 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-borrower-income.source_series_ids: Sum(Band Total Gross Income) ÷ Sum(Band Implied Borrowers) across TDTI bands
fhb-borrower-income.data_type: HLF-derived band-weighted mean from official RBNZ Table C41 bands
fhb-borrower-income.definition: The band-weighted mean annual gross borrower income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications and property investor applications, derived by HLF from RBNZ Table C41's Debt-to-Income bands.
fhb-borrower-income.calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232
fhb-borrower-income.formula: Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m]) ÷ Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m] ÷ Band Average Gross Income [$k]) × 1,000
fhb-borrower-income.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: RBNZ's Borrower Gross Income (BGI) measures total application income (which for couples combines two salaries, and for investors includes existing salaries plus gross rental and other qualifying income).
fhb-borrower-income.methodology: RBNZ Table C41 publishes official total gross income ($m, rounded to $0.1m) and average gross income ($000, rounded to $1,000) within each TDTI band rather than a single all-bands average. HLF derives the overall mean by dividing total gross income summed across all reported TDTI bands by the implied number of applications (Band Total Income ÷ Band Average Income) summed across those bands.
fhb-borrower-income.summary_text: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands).

kiwisaver-provider-switches.definition: The annual and average monthly number of KiwiSaver members transferring their account from one KiwiSaver scheme provider to another.
kiwisaver-provider-switches.formula: Monthly Average Transfers = Annual Scheme Transfers ÷ 12; YoY Change (%) = ((Transfers_t − Transfers_t-1) ÷ Transfers_t-1) × 100
kiwisaver-provider-switches.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Nearly 200,000 New Zealanders switch KiwiSaver providers each year as members review fees, long-term fund performance, and advice support.
kiwisaver-provider-switches.methodology: Sourced live from Inland Revenue's annual KiwiSaver scheme transfer release, dividing the annual transfer total by 12 for the monthly average and comparing against the prior financial year.
kiwisaver-provider-switches.summary_text: Over the year ended 30 June 2026, 198,897 KiwiSaver members switched providers (up 41.5% year-on-year from 140,557 in FY2016)—an average of 16,575 provider transfers per month.

kiwisaver-average-balance.html: As at 31 March 2026, total KiwiSaver funds under management reached $138.8B across 3.44 million members, with an average member balance of $40,340—up +213.9% (+12.1%/yr) from $12,852 in 2016 (+134.8%, or +8.9%/yr, after CPI inflation).
kiwisaver-average-balance.official_data_summary: FMA KiwiSaver Annual Report 2026 (year ended 31 March 2026, published 10 September 2026): Official average member balance = $40,340; Total FUM = $138.8B across 3.44m members (vs $12,852 / $33.8B in March 2016).
kiwisaver-average-balance.source_html:
HLF calculation: Nominal 10Y: ($40,340 − $12,852) ÷ $12,852 = +213.9% (+12.1%/yr) | Real 10Y (÷1.337 CPI): ($40,340 ÷ $17,183) − 1 = +134.8% (+8.9%/yr)
Source: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) — KiwiSaver Annual Report & RBNZ Table T43 • Direct RBNZ T43 .xlsx • Glossary: KiwiSaver First-Home Withdrawal • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

household-vs-individual-income-benchmark.html: In the June 2026 quarter, Stats NZ's Labour Market Statistics (Income) recorded median individual earnings of $1,419/week ($73,788/year) across wage and salary earners, $962/week ($50,024/year) across all people from all sources, and $959/week ($49,868/year) for self-employed individuals (with median full-time hourly earnings at $38.00/hour).
household-vs-individual-income-benchmark.official_data_summary: Stats NZ Labour Market Statistics Income (June 2026 quarter): Wage & salary median = $1,419/wk ($73,788/yr); All-source median = $962/wk ($50,024/yr).
household-vs-individual-income-benchmark.source_html:
HLF calculation: Wage & Salary Median: $1,419/wk × 52 = $73,788/yr | All-Source Individual Median: $962/wk × 52 = $50,024/yr | Self-Employed Median: $959/wk × 52 = $49,868/yr

household-vs-individual-income-benchmark.formula: Annualised Median Income = Official Stats NZ Median Weekly Income × 52 weeks
household-vs-individual-income-benchmark.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Gives solo earners an accurate individual income benchmark—preventing the distortion of comparing a single earner against two-earner household income totals.
household-vs-individual-income-benchmark.methodology: Extracted live from Stats NZ's Labour Market Statistics (Income) release, multiplying official median weekly earnings by 52 weeks to provide an apples-to-apples annual benchmark for solo earners.
household-vs-individual-income-benchmark.summary_text: In the June 2026 quarter, Stats NZ's Labour Market Statistics (Income) recorded median individual earnings of $1,419/week ($73,788/year) across wage and salary earners, $962/week ($50,024/year) across all people from all sources, and $959/week ($49,868/year) for self-employed individuals (with median full-time hourly earnings at $38.00/hour).
